target_customer: Local businesses such as doctors offices, later health centers, hospitals and government agencies that miss phone calls
problem: A large share of calls to small practices go unanswered and most callers do not leave voicemail, so appointments and revenue are lost; Hurricane Maria made reaching Puerto Rican doctors very hard.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for an AI phone and text receptionist (Lara)
product_category: AI receptionist and patient access platform

founders.name: Emmanuel Oquendo
founders.background_notes: Healthcare Brew says he co-founded BrainHi with Israel Figueroa in October 2017. Education not found in an opened source.

founders.name: Israel Figueroa Fontanez
founders.background_notes: Listed as CTO on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Phone and text conversational AI that schedules appointments and integrates with practice systems was standard but nontrivial in 2018 for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Conversational receptionist products were copyable, though healthcare compliance (HIPAA, SOC 2 later) and integrations create some lock-in.

incumbents: Answering services and virtual receptionist firms
takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; later Healthcare Brew describes a crowded field of well-funded startups.

market_need_then: Hurricane Maria in September 2017 disrupted communication with doctors offices in Puerto Rico; the company cites that 25 percent of calls to local businesses are missed and 80 percent of callers leave no voicemail (company claim).

branding.brand_signature: Lara, the named AI phone agent
branding.community_and_virality: Local press celebrated it as the first Puerto Rican startup accepted to Y Combinator in 2018.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a pun on hi plus brain but not explained by a source; local pride press in 2018 helped regional awareness only.

pivots.from: Automated receptionist for local businesses in Puerto Rico
pivots.to: Broader digital front door platform for health centers in Puerto Rico and the US mainland, plus government
pivots.why: Healthcare Brew says similar access problems were found in rural US areas; dates not stated.

outcome_analysis: BrainHi grew from a post hurricane receptionist idea into an AI patient access platform with hospital clients and claims of tens of millions of conversations. It is still active, but only a small seed round with no amount is verifiable, so its financial trajectory and scale of success cannot be judged.
notes: CB Insights shows about 250K total raised, unverified aggregator figure, not recorded. A pasquines.us 2018 article was blocked (403). Search snippets say the founders studied engineering at UPR Mayaguez but no opened source confirms it, so education is empty. No dated 2018 competitor source found; the list is empty.
